full_judgment:
Mr. Shahidul Islam J: By this Rule the Opposite Parties Nos. 1-4 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 21.9.2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna in Title Suit No. 156 of 1997 dismissing the suit brought under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders pass as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 "9. Suit by Persons Dispossessed of Immoveable Property: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immoveable property otherwise than in due cause of law; he or any person claiming through him may, by suit recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit. Nothing in this section shall bar any person from suing to establish his title to such property and to recover possession thereof No suit under this section shall be brought against the Government. No appeal shall lie from any order or decree passed in any suit instituted under this section, nor shall any review of any such order or decree be allowed,"' 

 10. In the result, the Rule is made absolute however, without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 21.9.2000 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Paikgacha, Khulna in Title Suit No. 156 of 1997 is hereby set aside. The suit is decreed, however without any order as to costs. The defendants are directed to hand over vacant possession within 1(one) month from the date of the decree failing which the plaintiff would be at liberty to get possession through process of the Court.
